game.name: Node: The Last Favor of the Antarii

items.text: Platformer Mode: NODE's steering has been rebuilt. Lane changes are now faster, cleaner and far more predictable, with no more overshooting the lane or getting stuck between lanes.
Platformer Mode: blocked lane changes (when something is in the way) now read much more clearly, with much less wobble and no leftover drift afterwards.
Fixed controls being reversed (pressing Left steering Right) after dying while travelling to the right.

Fixed NODE's head staying locked looking down after passing a checkpoint, when the thing it was looking at was no longer there.: Timeline Mode is unaffected by these changes. Plan execution behaves exactly as before.: Thank you to everyone who reported these issues, please keep the feedback coming :): Lapsus Games
Fixed on Steam Deck an issue that made the head of the drone look downwards during the first chapter
On Platformer Mode the drone now execute changes of orientation faster and cleaner
Fixed an issue that could prevent future Checkpoints if one of the has been partially jumped over.
Fixed an issue with the Epilogue's and Credits' font that failed to displayed properly all localized languages.
Fixed a place in Chapter 8 where you can end out of bounds.
General
The introduction slides now they're tighter and have the subtitles longer on display to make readability easier.: Audio
Underwater SFX volume fixed.
Re-balanced drone audio routing across explosions, cinematics, and key moments so effects sit correctly in the mix (no more drowned-out or misrouted sounds).
New rotating-sound effect for the GLAZ to help players infer from it what they're doing when outside of the screen.: Visuals
Camera improvements in some puzzles of Chapter 3&5 for cleaner framing.: Performance
Optimized the drone's volumetric light for smoother performance across all quality settings.
Eliminated a memory allocation hitch during menu/button navigation.: Puzzles & Levels
Adjusted a GLAZ puzzle and its setup for better flow.
Various small fixes and polish across levels.
Fixed an issue that the incorrect map would be displayed in Chapter 5 when playing in Spanish.
The UI now properly scales when using Nvidia DSR under window mode.
A small batch of fixes for the latest update.
Thank you to everyone who reported these issues. We appreciate your help!
Fixed a gap in the metallic floor just before the rooftop generator.
Dialogue boxes now maintain a top margin, preventing text from being cut off when messages are long.
NODE’s hand extension now triggers faster and more reliably.
Fixed a hard lock in Timeline Mode that could occur when resetting the game while holding the Freeze Time function.
Mouse cursor now correctly interacts with the UI after Alt+Tabbing out and back into the game while using DSR or other upscaling methods.
Steam Deck and virtual joystick inputs now trigger consistently once past the deadzone.
UI elements now properly deselect when the mouse becomes inactive or when switching input devices.
We're getting ready to release Patch 1.1 on May 28, alongside the Cerebral Puzzle Showcase. Before that, we wanted to say thank you.
A lot of what's in this update came directly from players. Messages, DMs, emails, reviews, conversations in our Discord. We read all of it.
So instead of just announcing the patch, we're letting you play it early.

notes.title: The build is password-protected. To access it

items.text: In your Steam library, right-click NODE: The Last Favor of the Antarii.
Select Properties, then the Betas tab.
Enter the access code: StoryModePlaytest
Select the Patch 1.1 branch from the dropdown.
Steam will download the beta build. Launch the game as normal.
Patch 1.1 goes public on Steam on May 28. The beta branch is Steam only; console patches are pending.
If you jump in, tell us what works, what does not, the best moments, and the rough edges.
We will be reading everything.
Lapsus Games

topNew: Some of you came to NODE for the atmosphere and story, but found the puzzles too intense to push through.

items.text: We have added an improvement to make the physics more stable and deterministic in low frame rate environments.

By popular request, we have added options to limit the frame rate of the game. Besides traditional Vsync, it can now be set to a fixed 60 or 30 FPS, or completely unlocked. (The new setting by default will be 60fps, since we found offers a great experience and gives more stability to the physics): Thank you all again for your continued support and feedback: Happy New Year :)
Fixed an issue introduced in the last patch where the Spanish localization made the game crash.
The game no longer crashes while changing the language, and it scrolls through Spanish.
Fixed an issue that caused checkpoints to be skipped after dying from a fall
The map can no longer be panned while on the paused menu

NODE now faces the correct facing direction on the saved game when the game is restarted.: The patch also includes some marginal performance increases.: Thank you to all who contributed with your feedback and comments, helping us improve the game :)
Fixed: Soft-lock on the electric panel repair.
Just a couple of small proactive fixes of things we found.
Fixed: Two puzzles where it was possible (even though improbable) to enter a soft-lock state.

Fixed: The possibility of triggering a jump at the very edge of a Checkpoint, triggering it, and at the same time never reaching it, making it possible to get a corrupt starting point for the puzzle: Thank you all: Lapsus Games
Small patch to address the vulnerability fix that Unity recently released.

Solved an issue that caused the state of some objects not to be saved correctly if the game was returned to the Main Menu and continued from there.: Thank you all for your continuous feedback and support: Lapsus Games
A couple of small fixes, but with a broad impact.

Now the position of NODE when reaching a Checkpoint is corrected on reset and loading to ensure no corrupt or broken state is permanent within a saved game. This will also fix the saved games of those affected by the issue. (If you see now a big difference between the execution on your first try vs the second, that means your original state wasn't correct, so "it is not a bug, it's a feature ;)"

Fixed some serialization issues when the OS was set to different regions that prevented the dialogues from being triggered correctly. This will also work on past saved games.: Thank you all for your continuous feedback and support: Lapsus Games
Thanks again to everyone for reporting issues and sending feedback. That way, we're able to fix it for everyone. These are the things that this patch fixes.

Possible Soft Lock while reaching the Checkpoint to repair the electric panel at the beginning of the game should be fixed now. That checkpoint will be harder to trigger by accident (don't try though XD)
Possible Soft Lock after speaking to PRIZMA for the first time has been eliminated.
Fixed sometimes you could slide NODE down a vertical wall without dying.
The Second Phase of the Crane won't allow you to go down a level and save the state of the cart in a different position.
The Steam Deck now features a slightly larger font size, Timeline, and UI scale to enhance readability.
Steam Deck now won't show Keyboard or Mouse controls when touching the screen. And its control panel has been specifically tailored to it.
Achievements now trigger correctly on Steam Deck
Thanks to your feedback, we addressed some of the bugs you have encountered and we also improved some accessibility issues with the default controls. Here is the list of changes:

When using Mouse and Keyboard, there are now two more options to change the decimal numbers on the commands. While hovering over the command to change, besides the scroll wheel, you can now use the Up and Down arrow keys, as well as the Middle and Right buttons for it.
A small sound effect that was causing issues during streamings on Twitch and YouTube has been substituted for one made in-house. No more muted sections on your uploads :)
The door near PRIZMA's server room cannot be closed by accident anymore, making the return more complicated than it should.

Please keep the suggestions and feedback coming and we'll do our best to address it as soon as we can. And if you're enjoying your experience with NODE, please don't forget to leave a positive Review. It helps a lot! :)
Lapsus Games

releases.displayName: NODE Development Update: Thanks for Your Feedback

items.text: After watching hundreds of you step into the ruins, solve puzzles, break our demo (thanks), and piece together NODE’s systems, we went back into the facility one last time.
We’re thrilled to announce that NODE is now complete!
Over the past few weeks, we’ve been making final adjustments and adding the last touches to elevate the experience — and now, the game is fully finished and ready for launch.
We’ve reimagined the opening of the game with brand-new custom art to better set the tone for your journey ahead.
NODE’s arrival in Toska now feels more grounded, with a stronger sense of place and purpose right from the start.
Conversations now include subtle voice cues from characters — not just for flavor, but to hint at the mood behind their words.
These ambient vocal touches bring an added layer of tension and personality to each exchange. Listen closely.
We’ve prepared a complete Dark Ambient Sci-Fi soundtrack, featuring over 50 tracks and more than 60 minutes of immersive audio.
The full OST will be available as part of a bundle at release, for those who want to spend more time in NODE’s atmosphere — even outside the game.

NODE is targeting a Q3 2025 release, and your support during this final stretch makes a huge difference. If you haven’t already, a wishlist goes a long way. Thank you again for playing the demo, sharing your feedback, and joining us on this journey. We’ll see you back in the facility!

releases.displayName: ⚙️ NODE Demo Update – Sharper, Smoother, Smarter

items.text: It’s been a few months since NODE’s first demo release. Since then, we’ve been quietly working, tweaking, testing, and tuning. Now that NODE is entering its polishing phase, it’s time to update the demo to better reflect where the game currently stands.

The demo is temporarily unavailable on Steam while we roll out this updated version. We know some of you were hoping to try it or revisit it sooner, and we appreciate your patience. It’ll be back, better than ever.

The biggest change? You can now carry your save file from the demo into the full game. Whether you like playing in long sessions or short bursts, NODE will meet you where you are. Start now, pick up later, your progress stays with you.

Every level in NODE was crafted with the story in mind. This update brings the earlier sections up to the visual fidelity of the rest. Atmosphere, lighting, and detail now better match the game’s tone. And yes, we’ve been squashing FPS drops along the way.
Things play smoother now. We’ve added quality-of-life updates:
Adjust game speed to skip downtime
Pause the timeline to read moments with precision
See exact second values instead of vague bars
More control = more satisfying problem-solving.
New to NODE? The updated intro includes helpful guidance for first-time players. It’s subtle, but effective. No hand-holding. Just what you need, when you need it.

notes.title: 🖥️ Polished UI, No Matter How You Play

items.text: We’ve overhauled the interface for clarity and comfort, whether you’re on a keyboard or gamepad. Smoother button feedback. Cleaner sound design. Small details, big difference.

NODE’s world has always been about precision and curiosity, and we’ve tried to carry that mindset into every update. Thanks to everyone who played the first version of the demo. Your feedback shaped this.
We’re making more improvements behind the scenes, stay tuned for the updated demo, coming soon.
Thanks to all the players for your feedback and bug reporting. We hope these changes make your journey "easier" :)

Now the Timeline has a Marker that remains at the point of the sequence when you die or you press Reset. This will give you a permanent place of reference to adjust your sequence until you execute it again.
While the Timeline executes you can hold "F" or the Left button on your Controller to accelerate time and skip forward the parts of the solution you don't need to adjust.
The map no longer drifts when additional controllers and joysticks are connected.
The Idle pose of the character returns to its normal state after resetting while colliding with something.
Fixed some rare cases where the execution of the same commands yields a different result.
The Commands duration can no longer be altered using the keyboard while the Timeline executes.
Fixed an issue that was contributing to frame drops while loading levels.
